{{日本の古墳 |名称=牽牛子塚古墳 |画像=[[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|280px]] |画像キャプション =墳丘全景（2022年） |所在地=[[奈良県]][[高市郡]][[明日香村]] |位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|27|58.7|N|135|47|32.29|E|region:JP-29}}| |形状=[[八角墳]] |規模=[[墳丘]]対辺長約22m（石敷・砂利敷部分を含むと32m） |築造時期=[[7世紀]]中葉-[[8世紀]]初頭 |被葬者=（一説）第37代[[斉明天皇]] |出土品=夾紵棺、[[七宝]]飾り金具、[[臼歯]]など |史跡=国の[[史跡]]「牽牛子塚古墳・越塚御門古墳」 |有形文化財 = 出土品（国の[[重要文化財]]） |地図2= {{Location map|Japan Nara|lat_deg=34|lat_min=27|lat_sec=58.7|lon_deg=135|lon_min=47|lon_sec=32.29|label=牽牛子塚
古墳|mark= 八角墳.svg|marksize=28|caption=|position=bottom|width=200|float=center}}| }} [[ファイル:220311 Kengoshiduka 3.jpg|thumb|250px|内部主体への通路(整備後)]] '''牽牛子塚古墳'''（けんごしづかこふん）は、[[奈良県]][[高市郡]][[明日香村]]大字越にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[八角墳]]。国の[[史跡]]に指定され、出土品は国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。 指定時には「あさがおつかこふん」の読みが付されており、「牽牛子」は[[アサガオ]]の別称である。「御前塚」と呼称されることもある[http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html 牽牛子塚古墳]奈良県明日香村。[[2009年]]（[[平成]]21年）から[[2010年]]（平成22年）にかけての[[発掘調査]]によって、[[八角墳]]（八角形墳）であることが判明し、[[飛鳥時代]]の[[女帝]]で[[天智天皇]]・[[天武天皇]]の母とされる第37代[[斉明天皇]]（第35代皇極天皇）の陵である可能性が高まっている。2022年2月に完全復旧が終了した飛鳥のアサガオ　奈良・牽牛子塚古墳、完全復元　毎日新聞 2022年3月3日 大阪朝刊。 == 立地 == [[橿原市]]との村境に近い[[明日香村]]大字越の[[丘陵]]先端部の一番幅広で、高所の安定した場所に位置しており、戸の古墳の墳頂部の標高は126.3メートルであり、国の[[史跡]]である[[岩屋山古墳]]（明日香村大字越）の西方約500メートルの地点に立地する。 == 外観・規模 == 以前より、巨石をくりぬいて2つの墓室を設けた特異な内部構造で知られており、斉明天皇（皇極天皇）と娘の[[間人皇女]]（[[孝徳天皇]]の[[皇后]]）の合葬墓とする説があった。また、[[1977年]]（[[昭和]]52年）から[[1978年]]（昭和53年）にかけて環境整備事業の一環として発掘調査がおこなわれており、その際、実際の[[測量]]をもとにした実測図が作成され、[[円墳]]と報告されながらも大塚・小林（1982）p.108-109八角墳の可能性が高いこともあわせて指摘されていた。 [[2009年]]9月より[[2010年]]9月にかけて、[[明日香村]][[教育委員会]]による学術目的の[[発掘調査]]がおこなわれ、2010年（平成22年）[[9月9日]]、村教育委員会は調査成果を発表した[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html 牽牛子塚古墳 斉明天皇陵と特定 八角構造が判明／奈良] 毎日新聞 2010年9月9日[https://web.archive.org/web/20100911212721/http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040072000c.html 牽牛子塚古墳：権威誇示 重量550トン、堅固な石の宮殿] 毎日新聞 2010年9月9日[http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686 墳丘は八角形、「斉明陵」強まる＝牽牛子塚古墳、発掘で確認―奈良・明日香村] 時事通信社 2010年9月9日。 それによれば、[[墳丘]]は[[地震]]により崩落していたが、高さ約4.5メートルと推定され、[[版築]]による三段築成の八角墳であることが判明し、墳丘の裾（すそ）は平面[[八角形]]状に削られており、対辺の長さは約22メートルにおよぶことを確認した。墳丘周囲では外側を八角形にかこむ[[配石遺構|石敷遺構]]が確認されており、[[北西]]の裾からは三辺分の石敷を検出している。うち一辺（約9メートル）はほぼ完全なかたちで遺存しており、幅は約1メートルで[[ブロック]]状の[[石|切り石]]が3列にすき間なく敷き詰められていた。石敷遺構そのものも、正八角形になるよう途中で約135度の角度で屈曲しており、上空から鳥瞰した場合、共通の中心をもち大きさの異なる、墳丘部分3段、[[平地]]の石敷部分3列の[[図形の相似|相似]]八角形が重なるかたちとなる。石敷の外側には、さらに[[砂利]]が敷き詰められ、その部分も含めると全体では32メートルほどの規模になると推定される。 また、[[三角柱]]状に削った白色[[凝灰岩]]の切り石やその破片が数百個以上出土しており、調査者は、これらの切り石は[[ピラミッド]]状に積み上げて墳丘斜面を装飾していたとしており、その総数は約7,200個におよぶと推定している朝日新聞 2010年9月10日。 墳丘一段目は一辺12.2メートル、対角線約33メートル、墳丘二段目は一辺約7メートル、対角線約18.5メートル、高さ4メートルである泉森皎「牽牛子塚古墳」 文化庁文化財保護部史跡研究会監修『図説 日本の史跡 第3巻 原始3』同朋舎出版 1991年 34ページ。 == 内部構造 == [[File:Kengoshizuka Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|石槨俯瞰図}}]] [[File:Kengoshizuka Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石槨展開図}}]] 内部施設は、南にむけて[[横穴式石室|横穴]]が開口するかたちの[[横口式石槨]]であり、2009年段階ではすでに一部露出していた。横口式石槨は、約80トンの重量をもつ1個の巨大な[[角礫岩|凝灰角礫岩]]をくりぬいて、約70トンの埋葬施設をつくったもので、巨石は約15キロメートル離れた[[二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)|二上山]]西麓より運搬したものと考えられる。石槨の幅は5メートル、奥行き3.5メートル、高さ2.5メートルの規模を有し、石槨内は中央部に幅44.7センチメートル、長さ152.5センチメートルの仕切り壁によって東西2つの空間に仕切られた合葬墳であることが判明した。刳りぬき部分の規模は、幅1.41メートル、高さ1.01メートル、長さ0.63メートルである。また、巨石の外側を取り囲むように丁寧な加工の施された[[直方体]]（縦2.7メートル、横1.2メートル、厚0.7メートル）をなす巨大な[[デイサイト]]製の切り石を3点確認し、本来的には16点整然とならんでいたであろうことも確認している。 石槨内の中央には間仕切りのための[[壁]]をともない、その両側に長さ約2メートルの墓室が2つあって、壁面は二重の[[漆喰]]が塗られている。左右両室ともに[[天井]]は丸みをおびており、高さはともに約1.3メートルである。また、左室は長さ2.1メートル、幅1.14メートル、右室は長さ2.08メートル、幅1.16メートルでほぼ同規模である。[[床]]面には長さ約1.95メートル、幅約0.78メートル、高さ0.08メートルの棺台（棺床）が削り出しによってつくられており、これも左右両室とも同一規模である。[[閉塞石]]は内扉と外扉より成っていて、内扉は[[凝灰岩]]製で高さ約1.12メートル、厚さ約0.62メートル、幅約1.47メートルであるのに対し、外扉は[[安山岩]]系の石材を用い、高さ約2.4メートル、厚さ約0.63メートル、幅約2.69メートルの大きさであった。また、内側の[[扉]]の四隅からは方形の孔（あな）を確認しており、扉飾金具が装填されていたことが推定される。 なお、古墳全体に使用された石の総重量は550トン以上と考えられる。運搬には[[丸太]]（ころ）を用いても数百人、[[地面]]を引きずったとすれば1,400人もの人員が必要であり、これについては、巨石を大勢で長距離運ぶこと自体に[[律令国家]]の[[権力]]を誇示する意図があったという見方がある。 ファイル:220311 Kengoshiduka 5.jpg|石槨外観（整備後） ファイル:Kengoshizuka sekisitsu L.JPG|石室内部左側 ファイル:Kengoshizuka sekisitsu C.JPG|石室内部中央 ファイル:Kengoshizuka sekisitsu R.JPG|石室内部右側 ファイル:牽牛子塚古墳 閉塞石.JPG|閉塞石 内扉 (明日香村埋蔵文化財展示室) == 出土遺物 == 以前の調査や採集によって、すでに[[夾紵棺]]（きょうちょかん）の破片や[[金銅]]製の棺[[金具]]（[[七宝]]亀甲形座金具、八花文座金具、六花文環座金具、円形座金具、綾隅金具）、また[[鉄]]製の鎹（[[カスガイ]]）、鉄製の[[釘]]、[[ガラス|ガラス玉]]などの[[玉]]類、人骨（[[臼歯]]）などの[[遺物]]が出土している。「夾紵棺」（きょうちょかん）とは麻布を[[漆]]で何重にも貼り重ねてつくった当時としては最高級の[[棺]]であり、[[貴人]]の[[葬送]]に用いられたことは疑いない。臼歯は間人皇女のものとの説がある。 [[1953年]]（[[昭和]]28年）[[11月14日]]、遺物は[[考古資料]]として極めて重要であるとして、一括して「大和国高市郡牽牛子塚古墳出土品」として国の[[重要文化財]]に指定され、指定分は[[奈良県立橿原考古学研究所]]附属博物館に保管されている。 ファイル:牽牛子塚古墳出土 七宝飾金具・金銅製八花形飾金具.JPG|七宝飾金具・金銅製八花形飾金具（国の重要文化財）
{{small|[[奈良県立橿原考古学研究所]]附属博物館展示。}} ファイル:AsukaTenjishitu Kengoshizuka02.jpg|七宝飾金具・棺金具・ガラス玉
{{small|明日香村埋蔵文化財展示室展示。}} ファイル:牽牛子塚古墳出土 夾紵棺片.JPG|夾紵棺残片（国の重要文化財）
{{small|奈良県立橿原考古学研究所附属博物館展示。}} ファイル:AsukaTenjishitu Kengoshizuka06.jpg|夾紵棺残片
{{small|明日香村埋蔵文化財展示室展示。}} == 遺跡性格 == [[ファイル:Oni no Manaita.JPG|thumb|150px|鬼の俎（明日香村野口）]] [[ファイル:Oni no Secchin.JPG|thumb|150px|鬼の雪隠（明日香村平田）]] [[ファイル:Masuda Iwafune.JPG|thumb|150px|益田岩船（橿原市）]] [[ファイル:Empress Kogyoku-Saimei.jpg|110px|right|thumb|斉明天皇]] === 時期 === 築造年代は、遺物等から[[7世紀]]後葉の年代が推定され、年代幅を広くとっても7世紀中葉から[[8世紀]]初頭までの範囲に収まる。 飛鳥地方の横口式石槨墳については、[[益田岩船]]（橿原市白橿町）や[[鬼の爼・鬼の雪隠]]（明日香村野口・同平田）の遺構が知られ、前者は本古墳と同じく刳り抜き式の横口式石槨、後二者は床石と蓋石が別々に構成されるタイプの石槨と考えられる。[[大阪府]][[寝屋川市]]に所在する[[石宝殿古墳]]の石槨は後者の類型に属するが、[[羨道]]をともなっており、そのことより、 *羨道をもつタイプ → 羨道をともなわないタイプ *床石と蓋石が別々に構成されるタイプ → 刳り抜きタイプ の[[編年]]が考えられる。つまり、石宝殿古墳の石槨は、このなかでは最も旧いことになる。 石材から年代を検討すると、益田岩船や鬼の爼・鬼の雪隠では硬質の[[石英閃緑岩]]が、本古墳では軟質の凝灰岩が使用される。飛鳥地方の他の古墳の事例からは、[[6世紀]]から7世紀中葉までは、やはり[[花崗岩]]等の硬質な石材、7世紀後半からは大阪・奈良の府県境にある二上山系の凝灰岩に推移する傾向がみてとれる。 以上を総合すると、飛鳥地方の横口式石槨墳は、 *鬼の爼・鬼の雪隠 → 益田岩船 → 牽牛子古墳 の先後関係が考えられる。 === 被葬者 === 斉明天皇の夫[[舒明天皇]]の陵墓（[[段ノ塚古墳]]）、子の[[天智天皇]]の陵墓（[[御廟野古墳]]）および[[天武天皇]]の陵墓（[[野口王墓]]、持統天皇との合葬墳）がいずれも八角墳であり、今回の精査によって、本古墳もまた当時の皇族の陵墓に特徴的な八角墳であることが確認されたこれについて、八角形は[[道教]]では「全世界」を意味することから死後も支配者であることを形状にこめたのではないかという見解がある。——[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040072000c.html?inb=yt 牽牛子塚古墳：権威誇示 重量550トン、堅固な石の宮殿]毎日新聞 2010年9月9日。また、本古墳が築造当初より合葬が明確に計画されていたことは調査成果によっていっそう明らかになった。さらに、加工石をこれほどふんだんに用いた[[古墳]]は他に類例がなく、古墳自体が巨大な石造[[記念物]]であることも明らかとなった。以前より知られていた夾紵棺や臼歯の存在、また『[[日本書紀]]』における斉明天皇・間人皇女合葬の記述とあわせて、本古墳が斉明天皇陵である可能性はさらに高まった。 いっぽう[[宮内庁]]は、本古墳から[[西南西]]の方向へ2.5キロメートル離れた、奈良県高市郡[[高取町]]大字車木に所在する[[車木ケンノウ古墳]]を斉明天皇陵として治定してきたため、おおかたの研究者との見解とのあいだに齟齬が生じている。そのため、真の[[継体天皇]]陵として有力視される[[今城塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[高槻市]]）や真の[[文武天皇]]陵として有力視される八角墳[[中尾山古墳]]（奈良県明日香村平田字中尾山）などと同様、従来の[[陵墓]]の治定を見直す必要があるのではないかという議論が起こっている。しかし、[[宮内庁書陵部]]では斉明天皇陵「越智崗上陵（おちのおかのえのみささぎ）」の候補地として牽牛子塚古墳が有力であるとする説があることを認めながらも、[[墓誌]]など確実なものが発見されない限りは陵墓治定を見直す必要はないとしている。 === 葬送者 === 『日本書紀』には、「天智天皇は、母である斉明天皇の命令を守り、大工事をしなかった」と記している。これは、被葬者を斉明天皇とみなすことについての慎重論の根拠たりうるが、被葬者が斉明天皇であるとした場合でも、葬送者は天智天皇ではないことの論拠ともなりうる。そのいっぽうで『[[続日本紀]]』には、斉明天皇陵（越智崗上陵）が「修造」されたとの記事が文武天皇3年（[[699年]]）のこととして記されており、この記載を根拠に、この年、斉明天皇が文武天皇により改葬されたのではないかと考える研究者もいる。なお、文武天皇は斉明天皇からみれば[[曾孫]]にあたる。 == 隣接する古墳の発見 == [[ファイル:220311 Kengoshiduka 4.jpg|thumb|250px|牽牛子塚古墳（奥）と越塚御門古墳（手前）]] 2010年12月9日、明日香村教育委員会は牽牛子塚古墳隣接地より古墳を検出したことを発表した。牽牛子塚古墳が斉明天皇の陵墓であるならば、新発見の[[越塚御門古墳]]は、斉明陵墓の前に孫の[[大田皇女]]を葬ったという『日本書紀』の記載より、大田皇女の墓である可能性が高い[https://web.archive.org/web/20101211190601/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/culture/news/20101209-OYT1T00770.htm 牽牛子塚古墳は斉明天皇陵か、実証の小古墳発見] 読売新聞 2010年12月9日。 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財（国指定） === * 大和国高市郡牽牛子塚古墳出土品 一括（考古資料） - 明細は以下。[[奈良県立橿原考古学研究所|奈良県立橿原考古学研究所附属博物館]]保管。1953年（昭和28年）11月14日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|9725|大和国高市郡牽牛子塚古墳出土品}}。 ** 七宝亀甲形金具 1箇 ** 金銅製八花形座金 1箇 ** 銅製金具残片 1箇 ** 乾漆棺残片 一括 === 国の史跡 === * 牽牛子塚古墳・越塚御門古墳 *: 1923年（大正12年）3月7日、「牽牛子塚古墳」の名称で国の史跡に指定。 *: 2014年（平成26年）3月18日、史跡範囲の追加指定、指定名称を「牽牛子塚古墳・越塚御門古墳」に変更。 *: 2015年（平成27年）10月7日、史跡範囲の追加指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1945|牽牛子塚古墳・越塚御門古墳}}。 == ギャラリー == ファイル:Kengoshizuka 6.jpg|牽牛子塚古墳(奥)と越塚御門古墳（手前）の模型。
{{small|古墳公園に設置。}} == アクセス == *[[近鉄吉野線]][[飛鳥駅]]より[[西北西]]約550メートル。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * {{Cite book|和書 |editor1=大塚初重|editor1-link=大塚初重|editor2=小林三郎|editor2-link=小林三郎 (考古学者) |title = 古墳辞典 |year = 1982 |publisher = [[東京堂出版]] |isbn = 4-490-10165-1 |page = }} == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Kengoshizuka Kofun}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1945|牽牛子塚古墳・越塚御門古墳}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|201|9725|大和国高市郡牽牛子塚古墳出土品}} * [http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html 牽牛子塚古墳] - 明日香村公式ウェブページ {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{デフォルトソート:けんこしつかこふん}} [[Category:奈良県の古墳]] [[Category:明日香村の歴史]] [[Category:八角墳]] [[Category:奈良県にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:奈良県の重要文化財]] [[Category:斉明天皇]]

{{日本の古墳 |名称=牽牛子塚古墳 |画像=[[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|280px]] |画像キャプション =墳丘全景（2022年） |所在地=[[奈良県]][[高市郡]][[明日香村]] |位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|27|58.7|N|135|47|32.29|E|region:JP-29}}| |形状=[[八角墳]] |規模=[[墳丘]]対辺長約22m（石敷・砂利敷部分を含むと32m） |築造時期=[[7世紀]]中葉-[[8世紀]]初頭 |被葬者=（一説）第37代[[斉明天皇]] |出土品=夾紵棺、[[七宝]]飾り金具、[[臼歯]]など |史跡=国の[[史跡]]「牽牛子塚古墳・越塚御門古墳」 |有形文化財 = 出土品（国の[[重要文化財]]） |地図2= {{Location map|Japan Nara|lat_deg=34|lat_min=27|lat_sec=58.7|lon_deg=135|lon_min=47|lon_sec=32.29|label=牽牛子塚
古墳|mark= 八角墳.svg|marksize=28|caption=|position=bottom|width=200|float=center}}| }} [[ファイル:220311 Kengoshiduka 3.jpg|thumb|250px|内部主体への通路(整備後)]] '''牽牛子塚古墳'''（けんごしづかこふん）は、[[奈良県]][[高市郡]][[明日香村]]大字越にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[八角墳]]。国の[[史跡]]に指定され、出土品は国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。 指定時には「あさがおつかこふん」の読みが付されており、「牽牛子」は[[アサガオ]]の別称である。「御前塚」と呼称されることもある[http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html 牽牛子塚古墳]奈良県明日香村。[[2009年]]（[[平成]]21年）から[[2010年]]（平成22年）にかけての[[発掘調査]]によって、[[八角墳]]（八角形墳）であることが判明し、[[飛鳥時代]]の[[女帝]]で[[天智天皇]]・[[天武天皇]]の母とされる第37代[[斉明天皇]]（第35代皇極天皇）の陵である可能性が高まっている。2022年2月に完全復旧が終了した飛鳥のアサガオ　奈良・牽牛子塚古墳、完全復元　毎日新聞 2022年3月3日 大阪朝刊。 == 立地 == [[橿原市]]との村境に近い[[明日香村]]大字越の[[丘陵]]先端部の一番幅広で、高所の安定した場所に位置しており、戸の古墳の墳頂部の標高は126.3メートルであり、国の[[史跡]]である[[岩屋山古墳]]（明日香村大字越）の西方約500メートルの地点に立地する。 == 外観・規模 == 以前より、巨石をくりぬいて2つの墓室を設けた特異な内部構造で知られており、斉明天皇（皇極天皇）と娘の[[間人皇女]]（[[孝徳天皇]]の[[皇后]]）の合葬墓とする説があった。また、[[1977年]]（[[昭和]]52年）から[[1978年]]（昭和53年）にかけて環境整備事業の一環として発掘調査がおこなわれており、その際、実際の[[測量]]をもとにした実測図が作成され、[[円墳]]と報告されながらも大塚・小林（1982）p.108-109八角墳の可能性が高いこともあわせて指摘されていた。 [[2009年]]9月より[[2010年]]9月にかけて、[[明日香村]][[教育委員会]]による学術目的の[[発掘調査]]がおこなわれ、2010年（平成22年）[[9月9日]]、村教育委員会は調査成果を発表した[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html 牽牛子塚古墳 斉明天皇陵と特定 八角構造が判明／奈良] 毎日新聞 2010年9月9日[https://web.archive.org/web/20100911212721/http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040072000c.html 牽牛子塚古墳：権威誇示 重量550トン、堅固な石の宮殿] 毎日新聞 2010年9月9日[http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686 墳丘は八角形、「斉明陵」強まる＝牽牛子塚古墳、発掘で確認―奈良・明日香村] 時事通信社 2010年9月9日。 それによれば、[[墳丘]]は[[地震]]により崩落していたが、高さ約4.5メートルと推定され、[[版築]]による三段築成の八角墳であることが判明し、墳丘の裾（すそ）は平面[[八角形]]状に削られており、対辺の長さは約22メートルにおよぶことを確認した。墳丘周囲では外側を八角形にかこむ[[配石遺構|石敷遺構]]が確認されており、[[北西]]の裾からは三辺分の石敷を検出している。うち一辺（約9メートル）はほぼ完全なかたちで遺存しており、幅は約1メートルで[[ブロック]]状の[[石|切り石]]が3列にすき間なく敷き詰められていた。石敷遺構そのものも、正八角形になるよう途中で約135度の角度で屈曲しており、上空から鳥瞰した場合、共通の中心をもち大きさの異なる、墳丘部分3段、[[平地]]の石敷部分3列の[[図形の相似|相似]]八角形が重なるかたちとなる。石敷の外側には、さらに[[砂利]]が敷き詰められ、その部分も含めると全体では32メートルほどの規模になると推定される。 また、[[三角柱]]状に削った白色[[凝灰岩]]の切り石やその破片が数百個以上出土しており、調査者は、これらの切り石は[[ピラミッド]]状に積み上げて墳丘斜面を装飾していたとしており、その総数は約7,200個におよぶと推定している朝日新聞 2010年9月10日。 墳丘一段目は一辺12.2メートル、対角線約33メートル、墳丘二段目は一辺約7メートル、対角線約18.5メートル、高さ4メートルである泉森皎「牽牛子塚古墳」 文化庁文化財保護部史跡研究会監修『図説 日本の史跡 第3巻 原始3』同朋舎出版 1991年 34ページ。 == 内部構造 == [[File:Kengoshizuka Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|石槨俯瞰図}}]] [[File:Kengoshizuka Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石槨展開図}}]] 内部施設は、南にむけて[[横穴式石室|横穴]]が開口するかたちの[[横口式石槨]]であり、2009年段階ではすでに一部露出していた。横口式石槨は、約80トンの重量をもつ1個の巨大な[[角礫岩|凝灰角礫岩]]をくりぬいて、約70トンの埋葬施設をつくったもので、巨石は約15キロメートル離れた[[二上山 (奈良県・大阪府)|二上山]]西麓より運搬したものと考えられる。石槨の幅は5メートル、奥行き3.5メートル、高さ2.5メートルの規模を有し、石槨内は中央部に幅44.7センチメートル、長さ152.5センチメートルの仕切り壁によって東西2つの空間に仕切られた合葬墳であることが判明した。刳りぬき部分の規模は、幅1.41メートル、高さ1.01メートル、長さ0.63メートルである。また、巨石の外側を取り囲むように丁寧な加工の施された[[直方体]]（縦2.7メートル、横1.2メートル、厚0.7メートル）をなす巨大な[[デイサイト]]製の切り石を3点確認し、本来的には16点整然とならんでいたであろうことも確認している。 石槨内の中央には間仕切りのための[[壁]]をともない、その両側に長さ約2メートルの墓室が2つあって、壁面は二重の[[漆喰]]が塗られている。左右両室ともに[[天井]]は丸みをおびており、高さはともに約1.3メートルである。また、左室は長さ2.1メートル、幅1.14メートル、右室は長さ2.08メートル、幅1.16メートルでほぼ同規模である。[[床]]面には長さ約1.95メートル、幅約0.78メートル、高さ0.08メートルの棺台（棺床）が削り出しによってつくられており、これも左右両室とも同一規模である。[[閉塞石]]は内扉と外扉より成っていて、内扉は[[凝灰岩]]製で高さ約1.12メートル、厚さ約0.62メートル、幅約1.47メートルであるのに対し、外扉は[[安山岩]]系の石材を用い、高さ約2.4メートル、厚さ約0.63メートル、幅約2.69メートルの大きさであった。また、内側の[[扉]]の四隅からは方形の孔（あな）を確認しており、扉飾金具が装填されていたことが推定される。 なお、古墳全体に使用された石の総重量は550トン以上と考えられる。運搬には[[丸太]]（ころ）を用いても数百人、[[地面]]を引きずったとすれば1,400人もの人員が必要であり、これについては、巨石を大勢で長距離運ぶこと自体に[[律令国家]]の[[権力]]を誇示する意図があったという見方がある。 ファイル:220311 Kengoshiduka 5.jpg|石槨外観（整備後） ファイル:Kengoshizuka sekisitsu L.JPG|石室内部左側 ファイル:Kengoshizuka sekisitsu C.JPG|石室内部中央 ファイル:Kengoshizuka sekisitsu R.JPG|石室内部右側 ファイル:牽牛子塚古墳 閉塞石.JPG|閉塞石 内扉 (明日香村埋蔵文化財展示室) == 出土遺物 == 以前の調査や採集によって、すでに[[夾紵棺]]（きょうちょかん）の破片や[[金銅]]製の棺[[金具]]（[[七宝]]亀甲形座金具、八花文座金具、六花文環座金具、円形座金具、綾隅金具）、また[[鉄]]製の鎹（[[カスガイ]]）、鉄製の[[釘]]、[[ガラス|ガラス玉]]などの[[玉]]類、人骨（[[臼歯]]）などの[[遺物]]が出土している。「夾紵棺」（きょうちょかん）とは麻布を[[漆]]で何重にも貼り重ねてつくった当時としては最高級の[[棺]]であり、[[貴人]]の[[葬送]]に用いられたことは疑いない。臼歯は間人皇女のものとの説がある。 [[1953年]]（[[昭和]]28年）[[11月14日]]、遺物は[[考古資料]]として極めて重要であるとして、一括して「大和国高市郡牽牛子塚古墳出土品」として国の[[重要文化財]]に指定され、指定分は[[奈良県立橿原考古学研究所]]附属博物館に保管されている。 ファイル:牽牛子塚古墳出土 七宝飾金具・金銅製八花形飾金具.JPG|七宝飾金具・金銅製八花形飾金具（国の重要文化財）

{{small|明日香村埋蔵文化財展示室展示。}} == 遺跡性格 == [[ファイル:Oni no Manaita.JPG|thumb|150px|鬼の俎（明日香村野口）]] [[ファイル:Oni no Secchin.JPG|thumb|150px|鬼の雪隠（明日香村平田）]] [[ファイル:Masuda Iwafune.JPG|thumb|150px|益田岩船（橿原市）]] [[ファイル:Empress Kogyoku-Saimei.jpg|110px|right|thumb|斉明天皇]] === 時期 === 築造年代は、遺物等から[[7世紀]]後葉の年代が推定され、年代幅を広くとっても7世紀中葉から[[8世紀]]初頭までの範囲に収まる。 飛鳥地方の横口式石槨墳については、[[益田岩船]]（橿原市白橿町）や[[鬼の爼・鬼の雪隠]]（明日香村野口・同平田）の遺構が知られ、前者は本古墳と同じく刳り抜き式の横口式石槨、後二者は床石と蓋石が別々に構成されるタイプの石槨と考えられる。[[大阪府]][[寝屋川市]]に所在する[[石宝殿古墳]]の石槨は後者の類型に属するが、[[羨道]]をともなっており、そのことより、 *羨道をもつタイプ → 羨道をともなわないタイプ *床石と蓋石が別々に構成されるタイプ → 刳り抜きタイプ の[[編年]]が考えられる。つまり、石宝殿古墳の石槨は、このなかでは最も旧いことになる。 石材から年代を検討すると、益田岩船や鬼の爼・鬼の雪隠では硬質の[[石英閃緑岩]]が、本古墳では軟質の凝灰岩が使用される。飛鳥地方の他の古墳の事例からは、[[6世紀]]から7世紀中葉までは、やはり[[花崗岩]]等の硬質な石材、7世紀後半からは大阪・奈良の府県境にある二上山系の凝灰岩に推移する傾向がみてとれる。 以上を総合すると、飛鳥地方の横口式石槨墳は、 *鬼の爼・鬼の雪隠 → 益田岩船 → 牽牛子古墳 の先後関係が考えられる。 === 被葬者 === 斉明天皇の夫[[舒明天皇]]の陵墓（[[段ノ塚古墳]]）、子の[[天智天皇]]の陵墓（[[御廟野古墳]]）および[[天武天皇]]の陵墓（[[野口王墓]]、持統天皇との合葬墳）がいずれも八角墳であり、今回の精査によって、本古墳もまた当時の皇族の陵墓に特徴的な八角墳であることが確認されたこれについて、八角形は[[道教]]では「全世界」を意味することから死後も支配者であることを形状にこめたのではないかという見解がある。——[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040072000c.html?inb=yt 牽牛子塚古墳：権威誇示 重量550トン、堅固な石の宮殿]毎日新聞 2010年9月9日。また、本古墳が築造当初より合葬が明確に計画されていたことは調査成果によっていっそう明らかになった。さらに、加工石をこれほどふんだんに用いた[[古墳]]は他に類例がなく、古墳自体が巨大な石造[[記念物]]であることも明らかとなった。以前より知られていた夾紵棺や臼歯の存在、また『[[日本書紀]]』における斉明天皇・間人皇女合葬の記述とあわせて、本古墳が斉明天皇陵である可能性はさらに高まった。 いっぽう[[宮内庁]]は、本古墳から[[西南西]]の方向へ2.5キロメートル離れた、奈良県高市郡[[高取町]]大字車木に所在する[[車木ケンノウ古墳]]を斉明天皇陵として治定してきたため、おおかたの研究者との見解とのあいだに齟齬が生じている。そのため、真の[[継体天皇]]陵として有力視される[[今城塚古墳]]（[[大阪府]][[高槻市]]）や真の[[文武天皇]]陵として有力視される八角墳[[中尾山古墳]]（奈良県明日香村平田字中尾山）などと同様、従来の[[陵墓]]の治定を見直す必要があるのではないかという議論が起こっている。しかし、[[宮内庁書陵部]]では斉明天皇陵「越智崗上陵（おちのおかのえのみささぎ）」の候補地として牽牛子塚古墳が有力であるとする説があることを認めながらも、[[墓誌]]など確実なものが発見されない限りは陵墓治定を見直す必要はないとしている。 === 葬送者 === 『日本書紀』には、「天智天皇は、母である斉明天皇の命令を守り、大工事をしなかった」と記している。これは、被葬者を斉明天皇とみなすことについての慎重論の根拠たりうるが、被葬者が斉明天皇であるとした場合でも、葬送者は天智天皇ではないことの論拠ともなりうる。そのいっぽうで『[[続日本紀]]』には、斉明天皇陵（越智崗上陵）が「修造」されたとの記事が文武天皇3年（[[699年]]）のこととして記されており、この記載を根拠に、この年、斉明天皇が文武天皇により改葬されたのではないかと考える研究者もいる。なお、文武天皇は斉明天皇からみれば[[曾孫]]にあたる。 == 隣接する古墳の発見 == [[ファイル:220311 Kengoshiduka 4.jpg|thumb|250px|牽牛子塚古墳（奥）と越塚御門古墳（手前）]] 2010年12月9日、明日香村教育委員会は牽牛子塚古墳隣接地より古墳を検出したことを発表した。牽牛子塚古墳が斉明天皇の陵墓であるならば、新発見の[[越塚御門古墳]]は、斉明陵墓の前に孫の[[大田皇女]]を葬ったという『日本書紀』の記載より、大田皇女の墓である可能性が高い[https://web.archive.org/web/20101211190601/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/culture/news/20101209-OYT1T00770.htm 牽牛子塚古墳は斉明天皇陵か、実証の小古墳発見] 読売新聞 2010年12月9日。 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財（国指定） === * 大和国高市郡牽牛子塚古墳出土品 一括（考古資料） - 明細は以下。[[奈良県立橿原考古学研究所|奈良県立橿原考古学研究所附属博物館]]保管。1953年（昭和28年）11月14日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|9725|大和国高市郡牽牛子塚古墳出土品}}。 ** 七宝亀甲形金具 1箇 ** 金銅製八花形座金 1箇 ** 銅製金具残片 1箇 ** 乾漆棺残片 一括 === 国の史跡 === * 牽牛子塚古墳・越塚御門古墳 *: 1923年（大正12年）3月7日、「牽牛子塚古墳」の名称で国の史跡に指定。 *: 2014年（平成26年）3月18日、史跡範囲の追加指定、指定名称を「牽牛子塚古墳・越塚御門古墳」に変更。 *: 2015年（平成27年）10月7日、史跡範囲の追加指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1945|牽牛子塚古墳・越塚御門古墳}}。 == ギャラリー == ファイル:Kengoshizuka It is said to be the burial site of [[Empress Kōgyoku]].{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}} it was reconstructed and opened to the public on May 6 2022. This contrasts with other Imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Gobyō-no-Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} which are closed to the public by the [[Imperial Household Agency]].{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) - Passage Grave in Japan in Honshū |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=The Megalithic Portal}} [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 3.jpg|thumb|Entrance to the burial chamber]] ==overview== '''Kengoshizuka Kofun''' (牽牛子塚古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}, Japan. It is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} and has been Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site. The excavated burial goods from the site are Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}}. The name "Kengoshizuka" includes the word "{{ill|Asagao|ja|アサガオ}}" ([[:en:Ipomoea_nil|Morning Glory]]), an alternate reading for "Kengoshi." The tumulus is also referred to as "Omae-zuka."[http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] Asuka Village Official Website Excavations conducted between 2009 and 2010 revealed that the tumulus was octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}, mother of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu}}. Full restoration was completed in February 2022.Nara's Asuka Morning Glory Kofun fully restored, "Mainichi Shimbun," March 3, 2022, Osaka Morning Edition == location == The tumulus is located near the border of {{ill|Kashihara|ja|橿原市}} and lies at the stable, broad apex of a hill in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. Its summit reaches an elevation of 126.3 meters and is approximately 500 meters west of the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}}, another National Historic Site. == Exterior and map_size == The site was previously known for its unique internal structure, consisting of two hollowed chambers within a massive stone. This led to theories that it served as a combined tomb for Empress Saimei and her daughter {{ill|Princess Hashihito|ja|間人皇女}} (consort of {{ill|Emperor Kōtoku|ja|孝徳天皇}}). Excavations in 1977–1978 created measured diagrams based on surveys, and while it was initially reported as a circular tumulus,Ōtsuka, Hatsushige, and Kobayashi, Saburō (1982). *Dictionary of Kofun.* Tokyo: Tōkyodō Publishing, pp. 108-109. the possibility of an octagonal structure was also noted. From September 2009 to September 2010, academic excavations by the Asuka Village Board of Education confirmed the octagonal layout.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: Confirmed as Octagonal burial and Likely burial Site of Empress Saimei.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040072000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: A 550-ton Stone Mausoleum Exhibiting Authority.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686 Octagonal Mound Confirmed for Kengoshizuka Kofun: Further Evidence of Empress Saimei's Tomb.] "Jiji Press," September 9, 2010. The mound was found to be a triple-tiered octagonal tumulus standing approximately 4.5 meters tall, with the base measuring 22 meters across. Surrounding the mound is a paved stone structure with a similar octagonal type, extending the total diameter to approximately 32 meters, including gravel layers. Hundreds of meticulously carved white tuff stones were uncovered, estimated to have originally numbered 7,200 and used to create a pyramid-like exterior.Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. == Interior burial == The interior is a {{ill|yokoguchi-style sekkaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}} (side-entry stone chamber), partially exposed as of 2009. The chamber is carved from a massive block of tuff weighing approximately 80 tons, sourced from [[:en:Mount_Nijō|Mount Nijō]] 15 kilometers away. The area of the chamber are 5 meters wide, 3.5 meters deep, and 2.5 meters high, divided into two spaces by a central partition wall. The total weight of the stones used in the construction exceeds 550 tons. Transporting such massive stones over long distances required significant manpower, highlighting the power of the centralized state. == burial goods == burial goods include lacquered coffin fragments, gold-copper fittings with {{ill|Cloisonné|ja|七宝}} patterns, glass beads, and human molars believed to belong to Princess Hashihito. These were Historic Site1 as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} in 1953.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|9725|牽牛子塚古墳Excavated Artifacts}} == Cultural Significance == The Kofun's unique octagonal type aligns it with other imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (tomb of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Noguchi Ouka Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (joint tomb of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}). This reinforces its probable identification as the tomb of Empress Saimei. == Adjacent Kofun == In December 2010, the Asuka Village Board of Education announced the discovery of a smaller kofun adjacent to Kengoshizuka Kofun. This nearby tomb, named {{ill|Kosotsukamikado Kofun|ja|越塚御門古墳}}, is hypothesized to be the tomb of Princess Ōta, Empress Saimei's gran11aughter.[https://web.archive.org/web/20101211190601/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/culture/news/20101209-OYT1T00770.htm Adjacent Tomb Likely Princess Ōta's burial Site.] Yomiuri Shimbun, December 9, 2010. == Access == * Approximately 550 meters northwest of {{ill|Asuka Station|ja|飛鳥駅}} ({{ill|Kintetsu Yoshino Line|ja|近鉄吉野線}}). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Kengoshizuka Kofun}} * [http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] - Mausoleum|mark={{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=}}.svg|marksize=28|caption=|position=bottom|width=200|float=center}} }} '''Kengoshizuka Kofun''' is a [[Kofun]] in [[Asuka, Nara]] Japan.Tokuse, Takahiko, and Eriko Oka. "Life in Archaeological Sites and Settlements in Asuka Village as a Model Case for Managing Settlements Adjacent to Archaeological Sites: A Proposal for the Future of Sa11ara." The journal of Center for the Global Study of Historic Site and Culture 2 (2015): 5-20.{{cite book |title=Kofuns in Europe and Japan: Comparative and Contextual Perspectives |date=30 September 2018 |doi=10.2307/j.ctv1228gf7|s2cid=240193791 }} Specifically, it is an [[Octagonal Kofun]]. It is said to be the burial site of [[Empress Kōgyoku]].{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}} it was reconstructed and opened to the public on May 6 2022. This contrasts with other Imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Gobyō-no-Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=}} which are closed to the public by the [[Imperial Household Agency]].{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) - Passage Grave in Japan in Honshū |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=The Megalithic Portal}} [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 3.jpg|thumb|Entrance to the burial chamber]] ==overview== '''Kengoshizuka Kofun''' (牽牛子塚古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]], Japan. It is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=}} and has been Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site. The excavated burial goods from the site are Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. The name "Kengoshizuka" includes the word "[[:en:Ipomoea nil|Asagao]]" ([[:en:Ipomoea_nil|Morning Glory]]), an alternate reading for "Kengoshi." The tumulus is also referred to as "Omae-zuka."[http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] Asuka Village Official Website Excavations conducted between 2009 and 2010 revealed that the tumulus was octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]], mother of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] and {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}}. Full restoration was completed in February 2022.Nara's Asuka Morning Glory Kofun fully restored, "Mainichi Shimbun," March 3, 2022, Osaka Morning Edition == location == The tumulus is located near the border of [[:en:Kashihara, Nara|Kashihara]] and lies at the stable, broad apex of a hill in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. Its summit reaches an elevation of 126.3 meters and is approximately 500 meters west of the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]], another National Historic Site. == Exterior and map_size == The site was previously known for its unique internal structure, consisting of two hollowed chambers within a massive stone. This led to theories that it served as a combined tomb for Empress Saimei and her daughter [[:en:Princess Hashihito|Princess Hashihito]] (consort of [[:en:Emperor Kōtoku|Emperor Kōtoku]]). Excavations in 1977–1978 created measured diagrams based on surveys, and while it was initially reported as a circular tumulus,Ōtsuka, Hatsushige, and Kobayashi, Saburō (1982). *Dictionary of Kofun.* Tokyo: Tōkyodō Publishing, pp. 108-109. the possibility of an octagonal structure was also noted. From September 2009 to September 2010, academic excavations by the Asuka Village Board of Education confirmed the octagonal layout.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: Confirmed as Octagonal burial and Likely burial Site of Empress Saimei.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040072000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: A 550-ton Stone Mausoleum Exhibiting Authority.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686 Octagonal Mound Confirmed for Kengoshizuka Kofun: Further Evidence of Empress Saimei's Tomb.] "Jiji Press," September 9, 2010. The mound was found to be a triple-tiered octagonal tumulus standing approximately 4.5 meters tall, with the base measuring 22 meters across. Surrounding the mound is a paved stone structure with a similar octagonal type, extending the total diameter to approximately 32 meters, including gravel layers. Hundreds of meticulously carved white tuff stones were uncovered, estimated to have originally numbered 7,200 and used to create a pyramid-like exterior.Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. == Interior burial == The interior is a {{ill|yokoguchi-style sekkaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoguchi-style sekkaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}} (side-entry stone chamber), partially exposed as of 2009. The chamber is carved from a massive block of tuff weighing approximately 80 tons, sourced from [[:en:Mount_Nijō|Mount Nijō]] 15 kilometers away. The area of the chamber are 5 meters wide, 3.5 meters deep, and 2.5 meters high, divided into two spaces by a central partition wall. The total weight of the stones used in the construction exceeds 550 tons. Transporting such massive stones over long distances required significant manpower, highlighting the power of the centralized state. == burial goods == burial goods include lacquered coffin fragments, gold-copper fittings with [[:en:Cloisonné|Cloisonné]] patterns, glass beads, and human molars believed to belong to Princess Hashihito. These were Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1953.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|9725|牽牛子塚古墳Excavated Artifacts}} == Cultural Significance == The Kofun's unique octagonal type aligns it with other imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=}} (tomb of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Ouka Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Ouka Tomb|qq=}} (joint tomb of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]). This reinforces its probable identification as the tomb of Empress Saimei. == Adjacent Kofun == In December 2010, the Asuka Village Board of Education announced the discovery of a smaller kofun adjacent to Kengoshizuka Kofun. This nearby tomb, named {{ill|Kosotsukamikado Kofun|ja|越塚御門古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kosotsukamikado Kofun|qq=}}, is hypothesized to be the tomb of Princess Ōta, Empress Saimei's gran11aughter.[https://web.archive.org/web/20101211190601/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/culture/news/20101209-OYT1T00770.htm Adjacent Tomb Likely Princess Ōta's burial Site.] Yomiuri Shimbun, December 9, 2010. == Access == * Approximately 550 meters northwest of [[:en:Asuka Station|Asuka Station]] ([[:en:Yoshino Line|Kintetsu Yoshino Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Kengoshizuka Kofun}} * [http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] - Mausoleum|mark={{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=}}.svg|marksize=28|caption=|position=bottom|width=200|float=center}} }} '''Kengoshizuka Kofun''' is a [[Kofun]] in [[Asuka, Nara]] Japan.Tokuse, Takahiko, and Eriko Oka. "Life in Archaeological Sites and Settlements in Asuka Village as a Model Case for Managing Settlements Adjacent to Archaeological Sites: A Proposal for the Future of Sa11ara." The journal of Center for the Global Study of Historic Site and Culture 2 (2015): 5-20.{{cite book |title=Kofuns in Europe and Japan: Comparative and Contextual Perspectives |date=30 September 2018 |doi=10.2307/j.ctv1228gf7|s2cid=240193791 }} Specifically, it is an [[Octagonal Kofun]]. It is said to be the burial site of [[Empress Kōgyoku]].{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}} it was reconstructed and opened to the public on May 6 2022. This contrasts with other Imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Gobyō-no-Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=}} which are closed to the public by the [[Imperial Household Agency]].{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) - Passage Grave in Japan in Honshū |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=The Megalithic Portal}} [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 3.jpg|thumb|Entrance to the burial chamber]] ==overview== '''Kengoshizuka Kofun''' (牽牛子塚古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]], Japan. It is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=}} and has been Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site. The excavated burial goods from the site are Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. The name "Kengoshizuka" includes the word "[[:en:Ipomoea nil|Asagao]]" ([[:en:Ipomoea_nil|Morning Glory]]), an alternate reading for "Kengoshi." The tumulus is also referred to as "Omae-zuka."[http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] Asuka Village Official Website Excavations conducted between 2009 and 2010 revealed that the tumulus was octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]], mother of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] and {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}}. Full restoration was completed in February 2022.Nara's Asuka Morning Glory Kofun fully restored, "Mainichi Shimbun," March 3, 2022, Osaka Morning Edition == location == The tumulus is located near the border of [[:en:Kashihara, Nara|Kashihara]] and lies at the stable, broad apex of a hill in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. Its summit reaches an elevation of 126.3 meters and is approximately 500 meters west of the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]], another National Historic Site. == Exterior and map_size == The site was previously known for its unique internal structure, consisting of two hollowed chambers within a massive stone. This led to theories that it served as a combined tomb for Empress Saimei and her daughter [[:en:Princess Hashihito|Princess Hashihito]] (consort of [[:en:Emperor Kōtoku|Emperor Kōtoku]]). Excavations in 1977–1978 created measured diagrams based on surveys, and while it was initially reported as a circular tumulus,Ōtsuka, Hatsushige, and Kobayashi, Saburō (1982). *Dictionary of Kofun.* Tokyo: Tōkyodō Publishing, pp. 108-109. the possibility of an octagonal structure was also noted. From September 2009 to September 2010, academic excavations by the Asuka Village Board of Education confirmed the octagonal layout.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: Confirmed as Octagonal burial and Likely burial Site of Empress Saimei.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040072000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: A 550-ton Stone Mausoleum Exhibiting Authority.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686 Octagonal Mound Confirmed for Kengoshizuka Kofun: Further Evidence of Empress Saimei's Tomb.] "Jiji Press," September 9, 2010. The mound was found to be a triple-tiered octagonal tumulus standing approximately 4.5 meters tall, with the base measuring 22 meters across. Surrounding the mound is a paved stone structure with a similar octagonal type, extending the total diameter to approximately 32 meters, including gravel layers. Hundreds of meticulously carved white tuff stones were uncovered, estimated to have originally numbered 7,200 and used to create a pyramid-like exterior.Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. == Interior burial == The interior is a {{ill|yokoguchi-style sekkaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoguchi-style sekkaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}} (side-entry stone chamber), partially exposed as of 2009. The chamber is carved from a massive block of tuff weighing approximately 80 tons, sourced from [[:en:Mount_Nijō|Mount Nijō]] 15 kilometers away. The area of the chamber are 5 meters wide, 3.5 meters deep, and 2.5 meters high, divided into two spaces by a central partition wall. The total weight of the stones used in the construction exceeds 550 tons. Transporting such massive stones over long distances required significant manpower, highlighting the power of the centralized state. == burial goods == burial goods include lacquered coffin fragments, gold-copper fittings with [[:en:Cloisonné|Cloisonné]] patterns, glass beads, and human molars believed to belong to Princess Hashihito. These were Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1953.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|9725|牽牛子塚古墳Excavated Artifacts}} == Cultural Significance == The Kofun's unique octagonal type aligns it with other imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=}} (tomb of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Ouka Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Ouka Tomb|qq=}} (joint tomb of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]). This reinforces its probable identification as the tomb of Empress Saimei. == Adjacent Kofun == In December 2010, the Asuka Village Board of Education announced the discovery of a smaller kofun adjacent to Kengoshizuka Kofun. This nearby tomb, named {{ill|Kosotsukamikado Kofun|ja|越塚御門古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kosotsukamikado Kofun|qq=}}, is hypothesized to be the tomb of Princess Ōta, Empress Saimei's gran11aughter.[https://web.archive.org/web/20101211190601/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/culture/news/20101209-OYT1T00770.htm Adjacent Tomb Likely Princess Ōta's burial Site.] Yomiuri Shimbun, December 9, 2010. == Access == * Approximately 550 meters northwest of [[:en:Asuka Station|Asuka Station]] ([[:en:Yoshino Line|Kintetsu Yoshino Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Kengoshizuka Kofun}} * [http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] - Asuka Village Official Website * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1945|牽牛子塚古墳・越塚御門古墳}} * {{国cultural property等データベース|201|9725|Yamato Province 高市郡牽牛子塚古墳Excavated Artifacts}} == References == {{Reflist}} Kengoshizuka Kofun {{Archaeology-stub}} {{Japan-stub}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|version=103767053|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:floating "of Japan"]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Nara Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Asuka, Nara]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:National Historic Sites in Japan]] [[Category:Empress Saimei]] [[Category:Kengoshizuka Kofun]] [[Category:Expanded pages from Wikipedia]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:Individual Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:imported Kofun]] [[Category:Pages goodbye $1 Wikipedia 3]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property (Japan)]] }} [[sn:Kengoshizuka Kofun]] [[ja:牽牛子塚古墳]] [[en:Kengoshizuka Kofun]] [[Category:奈良県にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:奈良県の古墳]] [[Category:奈良県の重要文化財]]

"Life in Archaeological Sites and Settlements in Asuka Village as a Model Case for Managing Settlements Adjacent to Archaeological Sites: A Proposal for the Future of Sa11ara." The journal of Center for the Global Study of Historic Site and Culture 2 (2015): 5-20.{{cite book |title=Kofuns in Europe and Japan: Comparative and Contextual Perspectives |date=30 September 2018 |doi=10.2307/j.ctv1228gf7|s2cid=240193791 }} Specifically, it is an [[Octagonal Kofun]]. It is said to be the burial site of [[Empress Kōgyoku]].{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}} it was reconstructed and opened to the public on May 6 2022. This contrasts with other Imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Gobyō-no-Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=}} which are closed to the public by the [[Imperial Household Agency]].{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) - Passage Grave in Japan in Honshū |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=The Megalithic Portal}} [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 3.jpg|thumb|Entrance to the burial chamber]] ==overview== '''Kengoshizuka Kofun''' (牽牛子塚古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]], Japan. It is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=}} and has been Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site. The excavated burial goods from the site are Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. The name "Kengoshizuka" includes the word "[[:en:Ipomoea nil|Asagao]]" ([[:en:Ipomoea_nil|Morning Glory]]), an alternate reading for "Kengoshi." The tumulus is also referred to as "Omae-zuka."[http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] Asuka Village Official Website Excavations conducted between 2009 and 2010 revealed that the tumulus was octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]], mother of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] and {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}}. Full restoration was completed in February 2022.Nara's Asuka Morning Glory Kofun fully restored, "Mainichi Shimbun," March 3, 2022, Osaka Morning Edition == location == The tumulus is located near the border of [[:en:Kashihara, Nara|Kashihara]] and lies at the stable, broad apex of a hill in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. Its summit reaches an elevation of 126.3 meters and is approximately 500 meters west of the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]], another National Historic Site. == Exterior and map_size == The site was previously known for its unique internal structure, consisting of two hollowed chambers within a massive stone. This led to theories that it served as a combined tomb for Empress Saimei and her daughter [[:en:Princess Hashihito|Princess Hashihito]] (consort of [[:en:Emperor Kōtoku|Emperor Kōtoku]]). Excavations in 1977–1978 created measured diagrams based on surveys, and while it was initially reported as a circular tumulus,Ōtsuka, Hatsushige, and Kobayashi, Saburō (1982). *Dictionary of Kofun.* Tokyo: Tōkyodō Publishing, pp. 108-109. the possibility of an octagonal structure was also noted. From September 2009 to September 2010, academic excavations by the Asuka Village Board of Education confirmed the octagonal layout.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: Confirmed as Octagonal burial and Likely burial Site of Empress Saimei.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040072000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: A 550-ton Stone Mausoleum Exhibiting Authority.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686 Octagonal Mound Confirmed for Kengoshizuka Kofun: Further Evidence of Empress Saimei's Tomb.] "Jiji Press," September 9, 2010. The mound was found to be a triple-tiered octagonal tumulus standing approximately 4.5 meters tall, with the base measuring 22 meters across. Surrounding the mound is a paved stone structure with a similar octagonal type, extending the total diameter to approximately 32 meters, including gravel layers. Hundreds of meticulously carved white tuff stones were uncovered, estimated to have originally numbered 7,200 and used to create a pyramid-like exterior.Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. == Interior burial == The interior is a {{ill|yokoguchi-style sekkaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoguchi-style sekkaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}} (side-entry stone chamber), partially exposed as of 2009. The chamber is carved from a massive block of tuff weighing approximately 80 tons, sourced from [[:en:Mount_Nijō|Mount Nijō]] 15 kilometers away. The area of the chamber are 5 meters wide, 3.5 meters deep, and 2.5 meters high, divided into two spaces by a central partition wall. The total weight of the stones used in the construction exceeds 550 tons. Transporting such massive stones over long distances required significant manpower, highlighting the power of the centralized state. == burial goods == burial goods include lacquered coffin fragments, gold-copper fittings with [[:en:Cloisonné|Cloisonné]] patterns, glass beads, and human molars believed to belong to Princess Hashihito. These were Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1953.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|9725|牽牛子塚古墳Excavated Artifacts}} == Cultural Significance == The Kofun's unique octagonal type aligns it with other imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=}} (tomb of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Ouka Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Ouka Tomb|qq=}} (joint tomb of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]). This reinforces its probable identification as the tomb of Empress Saimei. == Adjacent Kofun == In December 2010, the Asuka Village Board of Education announced the discovery of a smaller kofun adjacent to Kengoshizuka Kofun. This nearby tomb, named {{ill|Kosotsukamikado Kofun|ja|越塚御門古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kosotsukamikado Kofun|qq=}}, is hypothesized to be the tomb of Princess Ōta, Empress Saimei's gran11aughter.[https://web.archive.org/web/20101211190601/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/culture/news/20101209-OYT1T00770.htm Adjacent Tomb Likely Princess Ōta's burial Site.] Yomiuri Shimbun, December 9, 2010. == Access == * Approximately 550 meters northwest of [[:en:Asuka Station|Asuka Station]] ([[:en:Yoshino Line|Kintetsu Yoshino Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Kengoshizuka Kofun}} * [http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] - Asuka Village Official Website * {{国cultural property等データベース|401|1945|牽牛子塚古墳・越塚御門古墳}} * {{国cultural property等データベース|201|9725|Yamato Province 高市郡牽牛子塚古墳Excavated Artifacts}} == References == {{Reflist}} Kengoshizuka Kofun {{Archaeology-stub}} {{Japan-stub}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|version=103767053|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:floating "of Japan"]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Kofun in Nara Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Asuka, Nara]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:National Historic Sites in Japan]] [[Category:Empress Saimei]] [[Category:Kengoshizuka Kofun]] [[Category:Expanded pages from Wikipedia]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:Individual Kofun]] [[Category:Japanese imperial tombs]] [[Category:imported Kofun]] [[Category:Pages goodbye $1 Wikipedia 3]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property (Japan)]] }} [[sn:Kengoshizuka Kofun]] [[ja:牽牛子塚古墳]] [[en:Kengoshizuka Kofun]] [[Category:奈良県にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:奈良県の古墳]] [[Category:奈良県の重要文化財]] [[Category:斉明天皇]] [[Category:明日香村の歴史]]

From September 2009 to September 2010, academic excavations by the Asuka Village Board of Education confirmed the octagonal layout.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: Confirmed as Octagonal burial and Likely burial Site of Empress Saimei.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040072000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: A 550-ton Stone Mausoleum Exhibiting Authority.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686 Octagonal Mound Confirmed for Kengoshizuka Kofun: Further Evidence of Empress Saimei's Tomb.] "Jiji Press," September 9, 2010. The mound was found to be a triple-tiered octagonal tumulus standing approximately 4.5 meters tall, with the base measuring 22 meters across. Surrounding the mound is a paved stone structure with a similar octagonal type, extending the total diameter to approximately 32 meters, including gravel layers. Hundreds of meticulously carved white tuff stones were uncovered, estimated to have originally numbered 7,200 and used to create a pyramid-like exterior.Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. == Interior burial == The interior is a {{ill|yokoguchi-style sekkaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoguchi-style sekkaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}} (side-entry stone chamber), partially exposed as of 2009. The chamber is carved from a massive block of tuff weighing approximately 80 tons, sourced from [[:en:Mount_Nijō|Mount Nijō]] 15 kilometers away. The area of the chamber are 5 meters wide, 3.5 meters deep, and 2.5 meters high, divided into two spaces by a central partition wall. The total weight of the stones used in the construction exceeds 550 tons. Transporting such massive stones over long distances required significant manpower, highlighting the power of the centralized state. == burial goods == burial goods include lacquered coffin fragments, gold-copper fittings with [[:en:Cloisonné|Cloisonné]] patterns, glass beads, and human molars believed to belong to Princess Hashihito. It is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=}} and has been Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site. The excavated burial goods from the site are Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. The name "Kengoshizuka" includes the word "[[:en:Ipomoea nil|Asagao]]" ([[:en:Ipomoea_nil|Morning Glory]]), an alternate reading for "Kengoshi." The tumulus is also referred to as "Omae-zuka."[http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] Asuka Village Official Website Excavations conducted between 2009 and 2010 revealed that the tumulus was octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]], mother of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] and {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}}. Full restoration was completed in February 2022.Nara's Asuka Morning Glory Kofun fully restored, "Mainichi Shimbun," March 3, 2022, Osaka Morning Edition == location == The tumulus is located near the border of [[:en:Kashihara, Nara|Kashihara]] and lies at the stable, broad apex of a hill in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. Its summit reaches an elevation of 126.3 meters and is approximately 500 meters west of the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]], another National Historic Site. == Exterior and map_size == The site was previously known for its unique internal structure, consisting of two hollowed chambers within a massive stone. This led to theories that it served as a combined tomb for Empress Saimei and her daughter [[:en:Princess Hashihito|Princess Hashihito]] (consort of [[:en:Emperor Kōtoku|Emperor Kōtoku]]). Excavations in 1977–1978 created measured diagrams based on surveys, and while it was initially reported as a circular tumulus,Ōtsuka, Hatsushige, and Kobayashi, Saburō (1982). *Dictionary of Kofun.* Tokyo: Tōkyodō Publishing, pp. 108-109. the possibility of an octagonal structure was also noted. From September 2009 to September 2010, academic excavations by the Asuka Village Board of Education confirmed the octagonal layout.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: Confirmed as Octagonal burial and Likely burial Site of Empress Saimei.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040072000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: A 550-ton Stone Mausoleum Exhibiting Authority.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686 Octagonal Mound Confirmed for Kengoshizuka Kofun: Further Evidence of Empress Saimei's Tomb.] "Jiji Press," September 9, 2010. The mound was found to be a triple-tiered octagonal tumulus standing approximately 4.5 meters tall, with the base measuring 22 meters across. Surrounding the mound is a paved stone structure with a similar octagonal type, extending the total diameter to approximately 32 meters, including gravel layers. Hundreds of meticulously carved white tuff stones were uncovered, estimated to have originally numbered 7,200 and used to create a pyramid-like exterior.Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. == Interior burial == The interior is a {{ill|yokoguchi-style sekkaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoguchi-style sekkaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}} (side-entry stone chamber), partially exposed as of 2009. The chamber is carved from a massive block of tuff weighing approximately 80 tons, sourced from [[:en:Mount_Nijō|Mount Nijō]] 15 kilometers away. The area of the chamber are 5 meters wide, 3.5 meters deep, and 2.5 meters high, divided into two spaces by a central partition wall. The total weight of the stones used in the construction exceeds 550 tons. Transporting such massive stones over long distances required significant manpower, highlighting the power of the centralized state. == burial goods == burial goods include lacquered coffin fragments, gold-copper fittings with [[:en:Cloisonné|Cloisonné]] patterns, glass beads, and human molars believed to belong to Princess Hashihito. These were Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1953.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|9725|牽牛子塚古墳Excavated Artifacts}} == Cultural Significance == The Kofun's unique octagonal type aligns it with other imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=}} (tomb of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Ouka Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Ouka Tomb|qq=}} (joint tomb of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]). This reinforces its probable identification as the tomb of Empress Saimei. == Adjacent Kofun == In December 2010, the Asuka Village Board of Education announced the discovery of a smaller kofun adjacent to Kengoshizuka Kofun. This nearby tomb, named {{ill|Kosotsukamikado Kofun|ja|越塚御門古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kosotsukamikado Kofun|qq=}}, is hypothesized to be the tomb of Princess Ōta, Empress Saimei's gran11aughter.[https://web.archive.org/web/20101211190601/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/culture/news/20101209-OYT1T00770.htm Adjacent Tomb Likely Princess Ōta's burial Site.] Yomiuri Shimbun, December 9, 2010. == Access == * Approximately 550 meters northwest of [[:en:Asuka Station|Asuka Station]] ([[:en:Yoshino Line|Kintetsu Yoshino Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Kengoshizuka Kofun}} * [http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] - Mausoleum|mark={{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=}}.svg|marksize=28|caption=|position=bottom|width=200|float=center}} }} '''Kengoshizuka Kofun''' is a [[Kofun]] in [[Asuka, Nara]] Japan.Tokuse, Takahiko, and Eriko Oka. "Life in Archaeological Sites and Settlements in Asuka Village as a Model Case for Managing Settlements Adjacent to Archaeological Sites: A Proposal for the Future of Sa11ara." The journal of Center for the Global Study of Historic Site and Culture 2 (2015): 5-20.{{cite book |title=Kofuns in Europe and Japan: Comparative and Contextual Perspectives |date=30 September 2018 |doi=10.2307/j.ctv1228gf7|s2cid=240193791 }} Specifically, it is an [[Octagonal Kofun]]. It is said to be the burial site of [[Empress Kōgyoku]].{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}} it was reconstructed and opened to the public on May 6 2022. This contrasts with other Imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Gobyō-no-Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=}} which are closed to the public by the [[Imperial Household Agency]].{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) - Passage Grave in Japan in Honshū |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=The Megalithic Portal}} [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 3.jpg|thumb|Entrance to the burial chamber]] ==overview== '''Kengoshizuka Kofun''' (牽牛子塚古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]], Japan. It is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=}} and has been Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site. The excavated burial goods from the site are Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. The name "Kengoshizuka" includes the word "[[:en:Ipomoea nil|Asagao]]" ([[:en:Ipomoea_nil|Morning Glory]]), an alternate reading for "Kengoshi." The tumulus is also referred to as "Omae-zuka."[http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] Asuka Village Official Website Excavations conducted between 2009 and 2010 revealed that the tumulus was octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]], mother of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] and {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}}. Full restoration was completed in February 2022.Nara's Asuka Morning Glory Kofun fully restored, "Mainichi Shimbun," March 3, 2022, Osaka Morning Edition == location == The tumulus is located near the border of [[:en:Kashihara, Nara|Kashihara]] and lies at the stable, broad apex of a hill in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. Its summit reaches an elevation of 126.3 meters and is approximately 500 meters west of the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]], another National Historic Site. == Exterior and map_size == The site was previously known for its unique internal structure, consisting of two hollowed chambers within a massive stone. This led to theories that it served as a combined tomb for Empress Saimei and her daughter [[:en:Princess Hashihito|Princess Hashihito]] (consort of [[:en:Emperor Kōtoku|Emperor Kōtoku]]). Excavations in 1977–1978 created measured diagrams based on surveys, and while it was initially reported as a circular tumulus,Ōtsuka, Hatsushige, and Kobayashi, Saburō (1982). *Dictionary of Kofun.* Tokyo: Tōkyodō Publishing, pp. 108-109. the possibility of an octagonal structure was also noted. From September 2009 to September 2010, academic excavations by the Asuka Village Board of Education confirmed the octagonal layout.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: Confirmed as Octagonal burial and Likely burial Site of Empress Saimei.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040072000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: A 550-ton Stone Mausoleum Exhibiting Authority.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686 Octagonal Mound Confirmed for Kengoshizuka Kofun: Further Evidence of Empress Saimei's Tomb.] "Jiji Press," September 9, 2010. The mound was found to be a triple-tiered octagonal tumulus standing approximately 4.5 meters tall, with the base measuring 22 meters across. Surrounding the mound is a paved stone structure with a similar octagonal type, extending the total diameter to approximately 32 meters, including gravel layers. Hundreds of meticulously carved white tuff stones were uncovered, estimated to have originally numbered 7,200 and used to create a pyramid-like exterior.Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. == Interior burial == The interior is a {{ill|yokoguchi-style sekkaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoguchi-style sekkaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}} (side-entry stone chamber), partially exposed as of 2009. The chamber is carved from a massive block of tuff weighing approximately 80 tons, sourced from [[:en:Mount_Nijō|Mount Nijō]] 15 kilometers away. The area of the chamber are 5 meters wide, 3.5 meters deep, and 2.5 meters high, divided into two spaces by a central partition wall. The total weight of the stones used in the construction exceeds 550 tons. Transporting such massive stones over long distances required significant manpower, highlighting the power of the centralized state. == burial goods == burial goods include lacquered coffin fragments, gold-copper fittings with [[:en:Cloisonné|Cloisonné]] patterns, glass beads, and human molars believed to belong to Princess Hashihito. These were Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1953.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|9725|牽牛子塚古墳Excavated Artifacts}} == Cultural Significance == The Kofun's unique octagonal type aligns it with other imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=}} (tomb of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Ouka Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Ouka Tomb|qq=}} (joint tomb of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]). This reinforces its probable identification as the tomb of Empress Saimei. == Adjacent Kofun == In December 2010, the Asuka Village Board of Education announced the discovery of a smaller kofun adjacent to Kengoshizuka Kofun. This nearby tomb, named {{ill|Kosotsukamikado Kofun|ja|越塚御門古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kosotsukamikado Kofun|qq=}}, is hypothesized to be the tomb of Princess Ōta, Empress Saimei's gran11aughter.[https://web.archive.org/web/20101211190601/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/culture/news/20101209-OYT1T00770.htm Adjacent Tomb Likely Princess Ōta's burial Site.] Yomiuri Shimbun, December 9, 2010. == Access == * Approximately 550 meters northwest of [[:en:Asuka Station|Asuka Station]] ([[:en:Yoshino Line|Kintetsu Yoshino Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Kengoshizuka Kofun}} * [http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] - Mausoleum|mark={{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=}}.svg|marksize=28|caption=|position=bottom|width=200|float=center}} }} '''Kengoshizuka Kofun''' is a [[Kofun]] in [[Asuka, Nara]] Japan.Tokuse, Takahiko, and Eriko Oka. "Life in Archaeological Sites and Settlements in Asuka Village as a Model Case for Managing Settlements Adjacent to Archaeological Sites: A Proposal for the Future of Sa11ara." The journal of Center for the Global Study of Historic Site and Culture 2 (2015): 5-20.{{cite book |title=Kofuns in Europe and Japan: Comparative and Contextual Perspectives |date=30 September 2018 |doi=10.2307/j.ctv1228gf7|s2cid=240193791 }} Specifically, it is an [[Octagonal Kofun]]. It is said to be the burial site of [[Empress Kōgyoku]].{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}} it was reconstructed and opened to the public on May 6 2022. This contrasts with other Imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Gobyō-no-Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=}} which are closed to the public by the [[Imperial Household Agency]].{{Cite web |title=Gobyōyama Kofun (in Kyōto) - Passage Grave in Japan in Honshū |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=The Megalithic Portal}} [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 3.jpg|thumb|Entrance to the burial chamber]] ==overview== '''Kengoshizuka Kofun''' (牽牛子塚古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]], Japan. It is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=}} and has been Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site. The excavated burial goods from the site are Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. The name "Kengoshizuka" includes the word "[[:en:Ipomoea nil|Asagao]]" ([[:en:Ipomoea_nil|Morning Glory]]), an alternate reading for "Kengoshi." The tumulus is also referred to as "Omae-zuka."[http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] Asuka Village Official Website Excavations conducted between 2009 and 2010 revealed that the tumulus was octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]], mother of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] and {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}}. Full restoration was completed in February 2022.Nara's Asuka Morning Glory Kofun fully restored, "Mainichi Shimbun," March 3, 2022, Osaka Morning Edition == location == The tumulus is located near the border of [[:en:Kashihara, Nara|Kashihara]] and lies at the stable, broad apex of a hill in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. Its summit reaches an elevation of 126.3 meters and is approximately 500 meters west of the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]], another National Historic Site. == Exterior and map_size == The site was previously known for its unique internal structure, consisting of two hollowed chambers within a massive stone. This led to theories that it served as a combined tomb for Empress Saimei and her daughter [[:en:Princess Hashihito|Princess Hashihito]] (consort of [[:en:Emperor Kōtoku|Emperor Kōtoku]]). Excavations in 1977–1978 created measured diagrams based on surveys, and while it was initially reported as a circular tumulus,Ōtsuka, Hatsushige, and Kobayashi, Saburō (1982). *Dictionary of Kofun.* Tokyo: Tōkyodō Publishing, pp. 108-109. the possibility of an octagonal structure was also noted. From September 2009 to September 2010, academic excavations by the Asuka Village Board of Education confirmed the octagonal layout.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: Confirmed as Octagonal burial and Likely burial Site of Empress Saimei.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040072000c.html Kengoshizuka Kofun: A 550-ton Stone Mausoleum Exhibiting Authority.] "Mainichi Shimbun," September 9, 2010.[http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686 Octagonal Mound Confirmed for Kengoshizuka Kofun: Further Evidence of Empress Saimei's Tomb.] "Jiji Press," September 9, 2010. The mound was found to be a triple-tiered octagonal tumulus standing approximately 4.5 meters tall, with the base measuring 22 meters across. Surrounding the mound is a paved stone structure with a similar octagonal type, extending the total diameter to approximately 32 meters, including gravel layers. Hundreds of meticulously carved white tuff stones were uncovered, estimated to have originally numbered 7,200 and used to create a pyramid-like exterior.Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. == Interior burial == The interior is a {{ill|yokoguchi-style sekkaku|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yokoguchi-style sekkaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}} (side-entry stone chamber), partially exposed as of 2009. The chamber is carved from a massive block of tuff weighing approximately 80 tons, sourced from [[:en:Mount_Nijō|Mount Nijō]] 15 kilometers away. The area of the chamber are 5 meters wide, 3.5 meters deep, and 2.5 meters high, divided into two spaces by a central partition wall. The total weight of the stones used in the construction exceeds 550 tons. Transporting such massive stones over long distances required significant manpower, highlighting the power of the centralized state. == burial goods == burial goods include lacquered coffin fragments, gold-copper fittings with [[:en:Cloisonné|Cloisonné]] patterns, glass beads, and human molars believed to belong to Princess Hashihito. These were Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1953.{{国cultural property等データベース|201|9725|牽牛子塚古墳Excavated Artifacts}} == Cultural Significance == The Kofun's unique octagonal type aligns it with other imperial tombs such as the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=}} (tomb of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Ouka Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Ouka Tomb|qq=}} (joint tomb of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]). This reinforces its probable identification as the tomb of Empress Saimei. == Adjacent Kofun == In December 2010, the Asuka Village Board of Education announced the discovery of a smaller kofun adjacent to Kengoshizuka Kofun. This nearby tomb, named {{ill|Kosotsukamikado Kofun|ja|越塚御門古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kosotsukamikado Kofun|qq=}}, is hypothesized to be the tomb of Princess Ōta, Empress Saimei's gran11aughter.[https://web.archive.org/web/20101211190601/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/culture/news/20101209-OYT1T00770.htm Adjacent Tomb Likely Princess Ōta's burial Site.] Yomiuri Shimbun, December 9, 2010. == Access == * Approximately 550 meters northwest of [[:en:Asuka Station|Asuka Station]] ([[:en:Yoshino Line|Kintetsu Yoshino Line]]). == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Kengoshizuka Kofun}} * [http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] - It is an {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=}} and has been Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site. The excavated burial goods from the site are Historic Site1 as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. The name "Kengoshizuka" includes the word "[[:en:Ipomoea nil|Asagao]]" ([[:en:Ipomoea_nil|Morning Glory]]), an alternate reading for "Kengoshi." The tumulus is also referred to as "Omae-zuka."[http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html Kengoshizuka Kofun] Asuka Village Official Website Excavations conducted between 2009 and 2010 revealed that the tumulus was octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]], mother of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] and {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=}}. Full restoration was completed in February 2022.Nara's Asuka Morning Glory Kofun fully restored, "Mainichi Shimbun," March 3, 2022, Osaka Morning Edition == location == The tumulus is located near the border of [[:en:Kashihara, Nara|Kashihara]] and lies at the stable, broad apex of a hill in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. Its summit reaches an elevation of 126.3 meters and is approximately 500 meters west of the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]], another National Historic Site. == Exterior and map_size == The site was previously known for its unique internal structure, consisting of two hollowed chambers within a massive stone. This led to theories that it served as a combined tomb for Empress Saimei and her daughter [[:en:Princess Hashihito|Princess Hashihito]] (consort of [[:en:Emperor Kōtoku|Emperor Kōtoku]]). Excavations in 1977–1978 created measured diagrams based on surveys, and while it was initially reported as a circular tumulus,Ōtsuka, Hatsushige, and Kobayashi, Saburō (1982). *Dictionary of Kofun.* Tokyo: Tōkyodō Publishing, pp. 108-109. the possibility of an octagonal structure was also noted.
